text.p: Italian debt markets held to firmer levels near the day's highs after the Bonn government backed down on its plan to revalue the German central bank's assets in a bid to qualify for the start of Europe's single currency.

Dealers said that the market was still nervous and uncertain after the French Socialist victory on Sunday, and on future developments for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). Many believe that if EMU starts on time in 1999, it will have softer criteria than first planned.
"The German back down certainly helped BTPs, but the market is uncertain and awaiting any EMU news," one dealer said.

A source from the Bonn ruling coalition said that in the face of resistance from the Bundesbank, the revalution of 1997 was now no longer viable, but this would mean an further 10 billion marks to find to fill the hole in the 1997 budget.

Dealers said BTP futures started firmer following on from Monday's bounce back from earlier losses after the French election mark down was seen overdone, and then the German news helped most European bond markets to better levels.
"Although Italy now has a better chance of being in the first wave of EMU, fears of a EMU delay or softer terms will keep the market nervous," said the dealer.
Dealers added that the steady performance of the lira also helped to give the BTP market support with the lira last quoted in the 982 lire per mark area.
The June LIFFE future, which goes off the board on Wednesday, was up 66 basis points at 129.84 in late trade while the September contract was 102 basis points higher at 130.77.
